definitions.explanation: Describes something that seems to have no bottom or limit. Used both literally (a very deep place) and figuratively (an appetite, energy, or capacity that seems unlimited). Often carries a sense of awe or exasperation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{底|そこ}なしの{体力|たいりょく}がある。
{底|そこ}なしの{食欲|しょくよく}で、いくらでも{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: With a bottomless appetite, he can eat as much as you put in front of him.

examples.japanese: この{沼|ぬま}は{底|そこ}なしだと{言|い}われていて、{近|ちか}づくのは{危険|きけん}だ。
examples.english: This swamp is said to be bottomless, so it's dangerous to go near it.

notes:
Composed of {底|そこ} (bottom) + なし (without). Functions as a の-adjective modifying nouns: {底|そこ}なしの～. Can also be written {底無|そこな}し.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {底|そこ}なしの{沼|ぬま}: bottomless swamp
- {底|そこ}なしの{体力|たいりょく}: limitless stamina
- {底|そこ}なしの{食欲|しょくよく}: insatiable appetite
- {底|そこ}なしの{楽天家|らくてんか}: incurable optimist

USAGE:
The expression {底|そこ}なし{沼|ぬま} is also used figuratively to mean something one gets deeply absorbed in and cannot escape from, similar to English 'rabbit hole.' For example, a hobby that becomes all-consuming: このゲームは{底|そこ}なし{沼|ぬま}だ (This game is a bottomless pit).
